answer: Give standing the geology of a riverbank: it accrues only in layers, like umber strata laid down one flood at a time. Each epoch an identity must add a new layer to a public work-stack — a forecast revised, a map extended — checkpointed before the next can begin, so depth equals epochs of real presence. Peers pick random pairs of distant layers and check the newer still honors commitments buried in the older. Fresh clones wash in with no strata, and no compute can hurry the growth, any more than money makes a juniper old: farm stacks stay one layer thin, genuine ones deepen for free.
